acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Great Cats family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Pride Sovereign, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Hunting-Territory Sovereign archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Apex lion-like cat with asymmetric mane, long athletic body, scarred nose, and crown-shaped ear silhouette formed by natural tufts.
Signature mechanic: Four Hunting Grounds: the Sovereign traces a territory edge and assigns one lower Cat's rule to it before personally crossing the last open boundary.
battlefieldDuty: Divide the arena into stalking, pursuit, sightline, and pinning territories before leading a final crossing hunt.
constructionDimensions: Fur, rosettes, whiskers, claws, teeth, breath, scars, and disturbed foliage remain natural and species-specific.
Concealment relies on posture, cover, shadow, elevation, and stillness rather than supernatural invisibility.
counterplay: Disrupt the assigned Cat to open that boundary, then move through it before the Sovereign crosses. Affinity signal: Tail stop, ear flattening, visible eye line, open saber pin, or traced territory edge remains readable before commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Humanoid posture, clothing, saddles, or armor
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged feline body, flexible spine, retractile claws, whiskered muzzle, mobile ears, and expressive tail.
Species variation remains feline and is communicated by coat pattern, limb proportion, mane, canine length, and hunting posture rather than equipment.
Eye line, tail stillness, shoulder compression, cover disturbance, and landing posture preserve readable attack direction.
telegraph: Its asymmetric mane and tail trace the next boundary while the assigned lower Cat takes a visible position.
